_comment: Triage patterns ported from T3MP3ST src/recon/code-ingest.ts.
sink_evidence: the individual DANGEROUS_SINK_RE alternatives, each labeled, so
stage 1 can report WHICH sink matched. Their OR-union reproduces DANGEROUS_SINK_RE,
which is how deepen.py's attack-surface test is derived (no separate combined string
to drift out of sync). Case-sensitive, matching the source (no /i flag).
outbound_request / risky_params / security_controls / entry_point_* mirror the source
constants verbatim. Patterns listed in `case_insensitive` are compiled with re.IGNORECASE,
reproducing the source's /i flag on exactly those constants.
Python-precision divergence from the source: `httpx`, `urllib`, and `socket` now require a
call/attribute shape (`httpx\.\w+\(`, `urllib\.request`, `socket\.(socket|create_connection|
getaddrinfo|…)\(`) instead of the bare module name. The bare forms matched type annotations
(`x: httpx.Response`), imports, string literals (`"WebSockets (socket.io)"`), and domain
terminology (a dataflow framework's pipeline `socket` objects) as if they were call sites —
the top false positives on real Python codebases. Requiring a call trades a little
cross-language recall for far higher precision on the Python targets this skill aims at.
Recall divergence: the SQL sink is `\.execute\(` (any receiver), not the source's literal
`cursor\.execute`. Real code writes `c = conn.cursor(); c.execute(...)` or `session.execute(...)`,
so the identifier-bound form silently missed whole SQL-injection files at stage 1. The generic
form accepts a few benign `.execute(` calls in exchange for catching the injection sinks that matter.
Likewise `requests.*` covers all HTTP-method forms including the generic dispatch
`requests.request("GET", url)`, which the source's get/post/put-only pattern missed.
The bare-call sinks keep the source's `(?<![\w.])` guard (fixed-width negative lookbehind,
supported by Python re) so a C/JS free call `system(x)` matches but a method call
`foo.system(x)` does not — the guard was added deliberately to keep corpus rankings stable.
